slides.say: The operation diamond is defined for every number x. Diamond of x is equal to x squared. Diamond of diamond of five is equal to what?
So a diamond inside a diamond. The question is which one we do first. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, from the inside out, and then with the rule itself.

[short pause] Just like brackets inside brackets, we start with the inner one. The inner one is diamond of five. The diamond squares its input, so diamond of five is five squared, which is twenty-five.
at: we start with the inner one

slides.say: Now twenty-five takes the place of the whole inner diamond. So the outer diamond works on twenty-five. Twenty-five squared is twenty-five times twenty-five. Twenty times twenty-five is five hundred, and five times twenty-five is a hundred twenty-five. Together, six hundred twenty-five.

Careful, a lot of students stop after the inner diamond and mark twenty-five. But twenty-five is only halfway, because the outer diamond still has to work on it. So choice number one is the trap, and choice number three is our answer.
at: choice number one is the trap

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to see what two diamonds do to any number. The first diamond squares the number. The second diamond squares the result again. So we get x squared, all squared. x squared times x squared is x to the power of four.
So we need five to the power of four. Five squared is twenty-five, and twenty-five squared is six hundred twenty-five. Choice number three again. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: five to the power of four
